Migrating from predictmeans 1.x

Source: vignettes/migrating.Rmd
migrating.Rmd

Most scripts written for predictmeans 1.x run unchanged. This page lists what gives different numbers, what is new, and how to get the old results back.

library(predictmeans)
Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro * Variety + (1 | Block/Variety), data = Oats)

Results that change

Kenward–Roger adjusted standard errors are the default

For lmer models fitted by REML, standard errors, confidence limits, LSDs and p-values now use the Kenward–Roger adjusted covariance, as SAS DDFM=KR and emmeans do. In 1.x the unadjusted covariance was used with Kenward–Roger df. For balanced designs the two agree; for unbalanced ones the adjusted SEs are slightly larger.

To reproduce 1.x numbers, use vcov_adjust = FALSE:

Om <- Oats[-c(1, 2, 30), ]   # unbalanced
fm_u <- lmer(yield ~ nitro * Variety + (1 | Block/Variety), data = Om)
new <- predictmeans(fm_u, "Variety", plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
old <- predictmeans(fm_u, "Variety", vcov_adjust = FALSE, plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
cbind(SE_2.0 = new$means$std.error, SE_1.x = old$means$std.error)
#>        SE_2.0   SE_1.x
#> [1,] 8.086340 8.085432
#> [2,] 8.057580 8.057580
#> [3,] 8.138192 8.132226

Means that cannot be estimated are NA

A mean that depends on aliased (non-estimable) coefficients used to be printed as a number that depended on which coefficient R happened to drop. It is now NA, with a message; pairwise differences that are estimable are still shown. Means over empty cells keep the 1.x rule: the average of the observed cells, with a warning.

Permutation tests

permmodels() now uses Freedman–Lane permutations by default (method = "auto"): each term, coefficient or pair is tested with the model without it, so the other terms keep their effects. It also works for glm, glmer and glmmTMB models, and needs no refits. Mixed-model residuals are decorrelated with the symmetric square root of their covariance instead of the Cholesky factor, whose results depended on the order of the data. For the 1.x scheme use method = "raw"; its p-values for mixed models still differ slightly from 1.x because of the new square root.

Bugs fixed

Some 1.x results were wrong and are now correct, for example permlist together with atvar, a user-supplied Df for lmer models, factor levels containing ":", and several Kmatrix() cases with transformed covariates. See NEWS.md for the full list.

New in 2.0

  • Stable tables means, pairs and settings in every result, with as.data.frame(), tidy(), summary() and ggplot2::autoplot().
  • Degrees of freedom: df_method = "Kenward-Roger", "Satterthwaite" or "containment" (SAS DDFM=CONTAIN).
  • Averaging weights: weights = "proportional" (SAS OM), "outer", "cells", "flat".
  • specify_contrast() to write contrasts by the names of the means.
  • Covariates: Kmatrix() handles poly(), ns(), log(), smooth terms of gam and covariates that enter only through interactions; cov_reduce and exclude pass through predictmeans() and covariatemeans().
  • More comparisons: adj = "sidak", "scheffe" and "mvt" (exact single-step, as SAS ADJUST=SIMULATE); contrast_family() (Dunnett, polynomial trends, …); pm_joint() for joint F tests and slices; pm_slopes() for slopes by group; coef() and vcov() of the means. See vignette("contrasts").
  • Response scale: delta-method standard errors of back-transformed means, and ratios or odds ratios for log and logit models.
  • R2_model() (R² as numbers, Piepho or Nakagawa), bootmodels() (parametric bootstrap), and predictmeans() on semireg() fits.
  • Permutation tests for GLMs and GLMMs: permmodels() on the working scale, permlmer() (also permglmer(), permglmmTMB()) for nested GLMMs, and perms for permutations restricted by the design (permindex()). See vignette("resampling").
  • Other model classes can be added with a few methods (see ?pm_coef).
  • Fewer dependencies and faster Kenward–Roger and Satterthwaite computations.

Old and new output side by side

The 1.x list elements are still there, so code that reads pm$"Predicted Means" or pm$"Pairwise p-value" keeps working:

pm <- predictmeans(fm, "nitro", adj = "BH", plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
names(pm)
#>  [1] "Predicted Means"               "Standard Error of Means"      
#>  [3] "Standard Error of Differences" "LSD"                          
#>  [5] "Pairwise p-value"              "predictmeansPlot"             
#>  [7] "predictmeansBarPlot"           "mean_table"                   
#>  [9] "p_valueMatrix"                 "means"                        
#> [11] "pairs"                         "settings"
pm$`Predicted Means`
#> nitro
#>        0      0.2      0.4      0.6 
#>  79.3889  98.8889 114.2222 123.3889
pm$means
#>   nitro  estimate std.error       df  conf.low conf.high group  n estimable
#> 1     0  79.38889  7.174754 6.791824  62.31730  96.46047  A    18      TRUE
#> 2   0.2  98.88889  7.174754 6.791824  81.81730 115.96047   B   18      TRUE
#> 3   0.4 114.22222  7.174754 6.791824  97.15064 131.29381    C  18      TRUE
#> 4   0.6 123.38889  7.174754 6.791824 106.31730 140.46047     D 18      TRUE
